title: Data-Driven Reconstruction of Spatially Resolved Electron and Ion Energy Distributions from Macroscopic Plasma Quantities with Deep Neural Networks
abstract: arXiv:2608.16519v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Spatially resolved EEDFs/IEDFs provide essential kinetic information about low-temperature plasmas (LTPs) and play a central role in determining transport, chemical reaction rates, and plasma surface interactions. While kinetic simulations directly resolve these distributions, experimental measurements remain challenging and are often invasive, spatially limited, or require assumptions regarding the distribution shape such as a Maxwellian. However, several macroscopic plasma observables can be measured non-invasively using advanced diagnostic techniques, providing spatially resolved information about the plasma state. An important inverse problem is therefore whether readily measurable macroscopic plasma quantities contain sufficient information to reconstruct the underlying kinetic state. translated_title: 基于深度神经网络从宏观等离子体量数据重建空间分辨的电子和离子能量分布
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.16519v1 公告类型：交叉 摘要：空间分辨的电子能量分布函数（EEDFs）和离子能量分布函数（IEDFs）提供了低温等离子体（LTPs）的关键动力学信息，并在确定输运、化学反应速率和等离子体表面相互作用中发挥核心作用。虽然动力学模拟直接解析这些分布，但实验测量仍然具有挑战性，通常具有侵入性、空间局限性，或需要对分布形状（如麦克斯韦分布）做出假设。然而，使用先进诊断技术可以非侵入性地测量多种宏观等离子体可观测量，提供关于等离子体状态的空间分辨信息。因此，一个重要逆问题是：易于测量的宏观等离子体量是否包含足够信息来重建潜在的动力学状态。在本工作中，我们通过学习从空间分辨的宏观等离子体可观测量到相应动力学分布的非线性映射来研究此问题。
tldr: 本研究利用深度神经网络，从非侵入性测量的宏观等离子体量中重建空间分辨的电子和离子能量分布，解决了一个关键的逆问题。
en_tdlr: This work uses deep neural networks to reconstruct spatially resolved electron and ion energy distributions from non-invasively measured macroscopic plasma quantities, addressing a key inverse problem.
